outcome: Not settled in general. Since 26 January 2024 one further finite group, the Mathieu group M23, has been shown to be a Galois group over Q (Huang, Jackson, Lee, Poonen, Pries, Zhang, arXiv:2608.08538, v1 9 Aug 2026), completing the realisation of the 26 sporadic simple groups; a computational contest reports that all 25,000 transitive permutation groups of degree 24 were realised over Q (Paderborn press release, 10 Sep 2026; completion date disputed); and partial results for infinite families of simple groups and for other base fields appeared.
problem_asks: One question, read from the statement alone, with three parts: (1) the universal quantifier: every finite group G, not some or a restricted class; (2) the existence: for each such G, a Galois extension L/Q with Gal(L/Q) isomorphic to G; (3) the base field is Q specifically (not a number field, a function field, or Q(t)). The statement names nothing else: no degree bound, no explicit polynomials, no regularity condition, no parametric family. A result for one group settles part (2) for that group only; part (1) is the question as asked.

events.what_happened: Xiaoyu Huang, Blake Jackson, Kyu-Hwan Lee, Bjorn Poonen, Rachel Pries and Shaowu Zhang, 'The Mathieu group M23 is a Galois group over Q', arXiv:2608.08538. The arXiv listing gives v1 as Sunday 9 Aug 2026; the MIT-hosted PDF and MathWorld give 8 Aug. Abstract (as read through a summarising fetch of the arXiv HTML): 25 of the 26 sporadic groups were realised over Q during 1984-1989; the paper proves the last one, M23, occurs as a Galois group over Q, by producing an explicit degree-23 polynomial with rational coefficients whose splitting field has Galois group M23 over Q. Method: a non-rigid triple of conjugacy classes of M23, Belyi maps, and the numerical Belyi-map algorithm of Klug, Musty, Schiavone, Sijsling and Voight. Theorem 1.1 (v1, as read): 'There exists a Galois extension of Q with Galois group M23'; Theorem 1.3 (v1): 'There exists a regular Galois extension L/Q(t) with Galois group M23.' A specialisation gives an M22-extension of Q (v2 comments). Posted to arXiv, not yet in a journal as far as I could find.
events.revisions: v1 9 Aug 2026 (19 KB); v2 7 Oct 2026 (35 KB, current). v2 comments field, verbatim as returned by the fetch: 'Lots of additional information, 22 pages. Simpler equation for the regular M_23-extension of Q(t).'; 'More info about its specializations (bonus: a new realization of M_22 as a Galois group over Q).'; 'More info about coefficient recognition and rigorous Galois group computation.'; 'More info about the other six regular M_23-extensions over a degree 6 field arising from this Nielsen class.' I did not diff the versions; whether the explicit polynomial changed is shown only by the 'simpler equation' comment.
events.delivers: Existence of a Galois extension of Q with group M23, witnessed by an explicit degree-23 polynomial with rational coefficients (the coefficients were not retrieved by me). The construction goes through a regular M23-extension of Q(t) (Theorem 1.3, v1); the step from a regular extension of Q(t) to extensions of Q by Hilbert irreducibility is standard and is not spelled out in the sections I read, but the abstract states the Q-extension and the polynomial directly. Restriction: one finite group, M23, a sporadic simple group; no hypothesis is added. Side result: an M22-extension of Q (v2 comments).
events.remains: Every finite group other than the sporadic groups now realised; in particular all non-sporadic groups and the universal claim in part (1) of problem_asks. Nothing in the v1/v2 text I read addresses non-sporadic groups. With this event the sporadic groups are all realised over Q.
events.time_since_posted: about 2 months (9 Aug to 10 Oct 2026). I found no written mathematical reading by anyone outside the author team. The Epoch AI listing (see ai.sources and summary) is a status listing, not a reading of the argument.

machine_checked.system: Magma 2.29-9 and PARI/GP 2.17.4, used by the authors for the final verification (v2 acknowledgement, as read through the fetch; v1 names Magma and PARI/GP without versions). Not a proof assistant: I searched for a Lean or Coq formalisation of an M23 polynomial and found none.

events.directly_checkable: The degree-23 polynomial with rational coefficients: its Galois group and the field it cuts out can be recomputed in Magma or PARI/GP, and the Epoch AI problem asks for exactly such a polynomial. I did not retrieve the polynomial (the PDF was not decodable with my tools) and so did not check it.
events.doubts: No active doubt found. Points for the later pass to weigh, each with its basis: (1) the explicit polynomial changed between versions if the v2 comment 'Simpler equation for the regular M_23-extension of Q(t)' refers to the polynomial, so the v1 and v2 polynomials should be compared before either is taken as the record; (2) the v2 comment 'More info about coefficient recognition and rigorous Galois group computation' suggests the Galois-group verification was expanded in v2 (no correction is stated); (3) no external reading found in about two months; (4) Scientific American (22 Sep 2026) says AI agents searched for a geometric surface and new coordinates and that one agent produced the workable surface ('This might work!'), and the authors' text I read does not describe that step, so the account of how the key construction was found rests on press alone; (5) a search summary reported a leading-coefficient discrepancy between the arXiv listing and the MIT-hosted PDF polynomial; I could not confirm it, so it is unverified.
events.direction: Positive: asserts existence of a Galois extension of Q with group M23, i.e. the existence claim part (2) of the question asks for, for one of the groups it ranges over. No counterexample and no negative claim. It settles part (2) for one group and leaves part (1) untouched.
events.object: An explicit degree-23 polynomial with rational coefficients whose splitting field over Q has Galois group M23; the underlying object is a regular M23-extension of Q(t), from which the Q-extension is obtained by specialisation. Constructive, not a non-constructive existence proof: the authors computed Belyi maps for a non-rigid triple of conjugacy classes of M23 numerically (Klug, Musty, Schiavone, Sijsling, Voight algorithm), then recognised coefficients and computed the Galois group. The polynomial itself was not retrieved by me.
people: Xiaoyu Huang (Temple University, per press coverage)
Blake Jackson (affiliation given as Carnegie Mellon University in the Pittsburgh seminar abstract and as the Institute for Computer-Aided Reasoning in Mathematics in press coverage)
Shaowu Zhang (Caltech PhD student, per press coverage)

events.what_happened: Terence Tao, with John Jones, Jen Paulhus, David Roe and Andrew Sutherland, announced the third SAIR competition ('inverse Galois challenge') on his blog, 16 Jun 2026. Aim: numerical data for the degree-24 case of the inverse Galois problem, with the LMFDB; stage one brute-forces as many of the 25,000 transitive groups of degree 24 as possible and closes 15 Aug 2026; stage two targets groups that resist. The post says 'the unrestricted use of any sort of computational tool, including AI, to locate the polynomials, are expressly permitted'. Verification by MAGMA and PARI/GP rather than Lean. The Mathstodon repost (hackers.pub) quotes the phrase 'almost the first unsolved case' and excludes 'the notorious problem of whether the Mathieu group M23 is a Galois group'; that phrase does not appear in the blog text my fetch returned.
events.delivers: Nothing established. It is a call for computation, not a result. It targets finitely many instances: the 25,000 transitive permutation groups of degree 24.
events.remains: All of problem_asks. The call does not claim any realisation.
events.direction: Not a result; neutral. It is a computational project on finitely many instances of the universal question.

events.what_happened: University of Paderborn press release (10 Sep 2026) reports that Jurgen Kluners (Paderborn) and Gunter Malle (RPTU Kaiserslautern) won the 'IGP24 Competition' and that 'By July, all 25,000 groups – and thus the Inverse Galois Problem for degree 24 – had been completely solved'; the winners 'discovered more than 143,000 polynomials relevant to the problem'. Scientific American (22 Sep 2026) instead says 'The first phase of the competition concluded in late August, with all 25,000 relationships between polynomials and symmetry groups realized.' The two completion dates conflict; SAIR's own results page was not found. The first public written statement I found of the completion is the Paderborn release, so that is the date used here.
events.delivers: Per the press release only: an integer polynomial of degree 24 with each of the 25,000 transitive permutation groups of degree 24 as Galois group over Q. Restriction: this is a finite list of groups. It covers only finite groups that have a faithful transitive action of degree 24, and it says nothing about other finite groups. The release's 'the Inverse Galois Problem for degree 24' is its own label for this finite case, not the problem as stated. Polynomials not retrieved; the claim is not checked against SAIR's record.
events.remains: Every finite group that is not a transitive group of degree 24 and the universal claim in part (1) of problem_asks.

machine_checked.system: Magma and PARI/GP, as the contest rules state (Tao's post); I did not confirm which checks were applied to the reported results

events.directly_checkable: The integer polynomials themselves (the contest data, with LMFDB). Not retrieved.
events.doubts: The completion date conflicts between the Paderborn release ('By July') and Scientific American ('late August'); Tao's post set stage one to close on 15 Aug 2026. The press release's AI statements are mixed (see ai). The result is reported by a press release and a news article, not by SAIR or a paper.
events.direction: Positive for each of the 25,000 degree-24 transitive groups it covers (existence). It does not reach the general claim.
events.object: Integer polynomials of degree 24 realising each transitive group of degree 24 as a Galois group over Q; the Paderborn team reports more than 143,000 polynomials of this kind. Explicit polynomials, not non-constructive existence. None retrieved by me.
people: SAIR contest organisers (Tao, Jones, Paulhus, Roe, Sutherland)

events.what_happened: Julian Demeio and Damian Gvirtz-Chen, 'Galois Realisations of PSL2(F_{p^2}) via non-unirational Hilbert Irreducibility', arXiv:2512.23615, submitted 29 Dec 2025. Abstract (verbatim as far as the fetch returned it): 'We establish non-unirational versions of Hilbert Irreducibility for all Hilbert modular surfaces which are of K3 type. As an application we prove new instances of the regular Inverse Galois Problem for the simple groups PSL2(F_{p^2}) subject to congruence conditions on p.' Earlier talk (2023, search summary): work in progress.
events.revisions: v1 only (29 Dec 2025, 44 KB), per the arXiv abstract page as fetched.
events.delivers: New regular realisations (the standard meaning of 'regular' is over Q(t), which by Hilbert irreducibility gives extensions of Q) of the simple groups PSL2(F_{p^2}), for primes p satisfying congruence conditions that I did not retrieve. Restriction: one infinite family of simple groups, and only for p in those congruence classes.
events.remains: PSL2(F_{p^2}) for primes p outside the congruence conditions, and every other finite group, including all non-simple groups not covered by other results.
events.time_since_posted: about 9 months (29 Dec 2025 to 10 Oct 2026). A search snippet of the Glasgow eprint record (not opened) lists the work as not refereed.
events.direction: Positive for the groups it covers (existence over Q, via regular realisations).

events.what_happened: Christian Maire and Karim Sankara, 'On s-split p-Hilbert class field towers with prescribed Galois groups', arXiv:2508.07946. Abstract (first sentence, as read through the fetch): given a finite p-group G, a number field K with trivial p-class group, and a finite set S of primes of K, there is a finite extension F/K whose S-split p-Hilbert class field tower has Galois group G; the second sentence says this extends results of Ozaki and Hajir-Maire-Ramakrishna. A search summary reports a 2026 publication in the International Journal of Number Theory; not checked.
events.revisions: v1 11 Aug 2025 (15 KB); v2 6 Jul 2026 (29 KB, current).
events.delivers: Every finite p-group occurs as the Galois group of an S-split p-Hilbert class field tower over some finite extension of a number field K with trivial p-class group. Restriction: base field a number field K (not Q); the object is a tower of unramified extensions with splitting conditions, not a Galois extension of Q with a prescribed group; p-groups only.
events.remains: Everything in problem_asks: no finite group is realised over Q by this event. Discounted as a different question (analogue over number fields with tower and splitting conditions) under DEEP_DIVE section 2.1.
events.direction: Does not cut toward or against the question as asked: it realises p-groups over a different base field and tower.

events.what_happened: Aaron Landesman and Ishan Levy, 'Homological stability for Hurwitz spaces and applications', arXiv:2503.03861. Abstract (as read through the fetch): the homology of the Hurwitz space for any finite rack stabilises integrally; the dominant stable homology is computed after inverting finitely many primes, proving a conjecture of Ellenberg, Venkatesh and Westerland; applications to Malle's conjecture, the Picard rank conjecture and Cohen-Lenstra-Martinet heuristics. The count of G-extensions of F_q(t) for q large and coprime to |G| is described in talk abstracts (AHGT, Princeton/IAS), not in the arXiv abstract I read.
events.revisions: v1 5 Mar 2025 (117 KB); v2 1 Oct 2025 (121 KB, current).
events.delivers: Stable-homology results for Hurwitz spaces and, as applications, results on Malle's conjecture over function fields F_q(t) (for q large and coprime to |G|, per talk abstracts). Restriction: function fields of characteristic p, not Q.
events.remains: Everything in problem_asks: no extension of Q is produced. Discounted as a different question (function fields over finite fields) under DEEP_DIVE section 2.1.
events.direction: Does not cut toward or against the question as asked: it concerns function fields over finite fields.

events.what_happened: Pierre Debes, 'Hurwitz spaces and Inverse Galois Theory', arXiv:2601.06532. Abstract (as read through the fetch): a survey of about fifty years of work on Hurwitz spaces in inverse Galois theory, covering 1990-2010 and recent results on the ring of components, including constructing components defined over Q and applying the Ellenberg-Venkatesh-Westerland approach to rational points over finite fields.
events.revisions: v1 10 Jan 2026 (61 KB); v2 11 Apr 2026 (53 KB, current).
events.delivers: No new theorem is claimed in the abstract. It surveys the Hurwitz-space route to the problem and reports constructions of components defined over Q.
events.remains: All of problem_asks. Recorded as context: a survey, not a resolution.
events.direction: Neutral: a survey.

events.what_happened: David Zywina, 'The inverse Galois problem for PSL_2(F_p)', arXiv:1303.3646, v1 15 Mar 2013. Abstract (as read through the fetch): 'We show that the simple group PSL_2(F_p) occurs as the Galois group of an extension of the rationals for all primes p>3', obtained by studying the Galois action on the second etale cohomology of a specific elliptic surface. Search summaries report earlier partial results (Shih 1974; a case from Malle; Clark) that this closes.
events.revisions: v1 15 Mar 2013; later versions not checked.
events.delivers: Every PSL2(F_p) with p>3 (equivalently p>=5) occurs as a Galois group over Q. Restriction: one family of simple groups.
events.remains: Every other finite group, including non-simple groups and simple groups outside this family.
events.direction: Positive for the family it covers.

events.what_happened: David Zywina, 'The inverse Galois problem for orthogonal groups', arXiv:1409.1151, v1 3 Sep 2014. Abstract (as read through the fetch): Omega_{2n+1}(p) and POmega+_{4n}(p) occur as Galois groups over the rationals for all n > 1 and all primes p > 3, via families of twists of elliptic curves, some known cases of the Birch and Swinnerton-Dyer conjecture, and a big monodromy result of Hall.
events.revisions: v1 3 Sep 2014; later versions not checked.
events.delivers: Infinitely many simple orthogonal-type groups over Q (two families, for n > 1 and primes p > 3).
events.remains: Every other finite group, including other families of simple groups.
events.direction: Positive for the families it covers.

events.what_happened: Michael Dettweiler and Stefan Reiter, 'On Galois realizations of special linear groups', arXiv:2309.14115, v1 25 Sep 2023 (only version listed). Abstract (as read through the fetch): studies the determinant of certain etale sheaves built by middle convolution to realise special linear groups 'regularly as Galois groups over the rationals'. A search summary describes the realisation as regular over Q(t); the fetched abstract page says 'over the rationals', so the base is not settled by what I read.
events.revisions: v1 25 Sep 2023 only, per arXiv listing.
events.delivers: Special linear groups SL_n(F_q) realised regularly over the rationals, for the range of n and q I did not retrieve.
events.remains: Every other finite group, including PSL/PGL and other finite groups outside the SL family and its range.
events.doubts: Base field unsettled between sources (see event). Range of n and q not retrieved.
events.direction: Positive for the groups it covers.

events.what_happened: Pierre Debes, 'Groups with no Parametric Galois Extension', arXiv:1605.09363, v1 30 May 2016. Abstract (paraphrased in the fetch; the summary says it disproves a strong form of the Regular Inverse Galois Problem): some finite groups (S_n for n>=7, infinitely many PSL2(F_p), the Monster) have no parametric realisation over Q(U) that induces all Galois extensions of Q(U) of that group; the analogous question over Q is addressed under a diophantine hypothesis related to a problem of Schinzel.
events.revisions: v1 30 May 2016; later versions not checked.
events.delivers: A negative result about a strong form (parametric realisations inducing all extensions over Q(U)) of the regular problem. It does not show any finite group fails to be a Galois group over Q. The Q-version is conditional on a diophantine hypothesis.
events.remains: All of problem_asks as stated; the negative result concerns a stronger form.
events.direction: Negative, but about a strong or parametric form, not about the bullet's existence question. Recorded as a discounted event under DEEP_DIVE section 2.1.

events.what_happened: Noam Elkies, computation of degree-23 polynomials with Galois group M23 over a number field (near miss). Presented at ANTS-X (2012) and published in the Open Book Series vol. 1 (2013), pp. 18-. The M23 paper's introduction (v1, as read through the fetch) says Elkies 'computed four degree-23 polynomials whose coefficients lie in a degree-4 number field'. Search summaries add that the field contains Q(sqrt(-23)) and is generated by a root of g^4+g^3+9g^2-10g+8 (not opened). These are polynomials over a number field, not over Q.
events.delivers: M23 as the Galois group of degree-23 polynomials over a degree-4 number field (or over C(t), geometrically), not over Q.
events.remains: The Q-question for M23 (this event does not establish a Galois extension of Q).
events.direction: Partial: positive over a different base field. Discounted for the Q-question under DEEP_DIVE section 2.1.
events.object: Four equivalence classes of degree-23 complex polynomials with Galois group M23, each with coefficients in a degree-4 number field (per the M23 paper's introduction; the explicit polynomials were not retrieved).

events.what_happened: Earlier M23-extensions over other fields, as listed in the introduction of the 2026 paper (v1, read through the fetch): Hoyden-Siedersleben and Hafner obtained M23-extensions over Q(sqrt(-23)) and Q(sqrt(-7)) from regular M24-extensions; Granboulan built one over fields containing the points of a conic that has no rational point. Dates and journal references for these were not established by me.
events.delivers: M23-extensions over quadratic fields Q(sqrt(-23)) and Q(sqrt(-7)), and over a conic's function field; none over Q.
events.remains: The Q-question for M23 (not settled by these).
events.direction: Partial results over other fields. Discounted for the Q-question.

events.what_happened: Thompson (1984) showed the Monster occurs as a Galois group over Q, and rigidity-method work from 1984 to 1989 realised 25 of the 26 sporadic simple groups over Q (per the abstract of the 2026 M23 paper and the Pittsburgh seminar abstract, both read). M23 was the holdout until 2026. Individual attributions for the other groups (Matzat, Malle and others, per search summaries) and the journal references were not verified.
events.delivers: 24 of the 26 sporadic simple groups excluding M23 (25 including the Monster) realised over Q.
events.remains: M23, until event huang-et-al-2026-m23; and every non-sporadic finite group.
events.direction: Positive for the sporadic groups it covers.

Ann. 207 (1974), 99-120 (citation as given in a search summary; not opened; the search hit that carries the citation is arXiv math/0506490, also not opened). Result per the summary: PSL2(F_p) occurs as a Galois group over Q when 2, 3 or 7 is a quadratic non-residue mod p.

events.delivers: Every finite p-group for odd primes p, over Q.
events.remains: Groups that are not p-groups for odd p.
events.direction: Positive for the class it covers.

events.what_happened: Shafarevich: every finite solvable group occurs as a Galois group over Q (stated on the Wikipedia article, read; the 1954 date for the Izvestiya paper is from a search summary, not opened). Schmidt and Wingberg (1999 preprint, page opened) describe their work as 'a complete proof of I.R. Safarevic's famous theorem that every finite solvable group occurs as a Galois group over Q', which implies the original argument was incomplete. A search summary says the gap concerned the prime 2 and was repaired; the page I opened does not mention a gap, so that is unverified.

events.remains: Non-solvable finite groups, including non-abelian simple groups not already covered, and the universal claim.
events.doubts: The original argument's gap at the prime 2 (per search summary, unverified); Schmidt and Wingberg's 1999 preprint is described as giving the complete proof.
events.direction: Positive for the solvable groups it covers.

events.what_happened: Hilbert (1892), via his irreducibility theorem: the symmetric groups S_n and alternating groups A_n occur as Galois groups over Q for every n>=1 (per search summaries; the primary paper was not opened). Schur (1930) gave explicit polynomials for A_n (search summary).
events.delivers: S_n and A_n over Q, for every n.
events.remains: All other finite groups.
events.direction: Positive for the groups it covers.

events.what_happened: Lukasz Matysiak, 'The Inverse Galois Problem', J. Appl. Math. & Informatics 40 (2022), 765-767 (citation as given in a search summary; the PDF was not decodable with my tools). Abstract, as reported in a search summary: it presents 'the proof that any group G is a Galois group of any field extension' as the solution of the inverse Galois problem. A 2023 paper by the same author (Carpathian Math. Publ., search summary only) repeats a weaker 'some field' version.
events.delivers: As the abstract is reported, a solution of the universal problem for every field. The literal claim is false: over a fixed field such as R, not every group occurs (the finite Galois extensions of R are R and C, so only groups of order at most 2 occur; this check is my own). The weaker 'some field' statement is standard and does not address Q.
events.remains: All of problem_asks for Q.
events.time_since_posted: about 4 years (2022 to 2026). My searches found no published critique or erratum.
events.doubts: The reported claim is false as stated (fails over R, by a check I did myself) and conflicts with the open status of the problem recorded on Wikipedia and Epoch AI. The PDF was not read, so the argument itself is unchecked.
events.direction: Claims the answer is yes for every field; as stated, cuts against the literal claim. Discounted: the scope is 'any field', not Q, and the claim is wrong as stated.

disputes.summary: Who found the M23 construction and how. Scientific American (22 Sep 2026, read directly) says the team 'set a raft of AI agents to work on new, more harmonious coordinates' and that one agent reported 'This might work!' about one of seven surfaces; humans then turned the surface into equations. The authors' acknowledgements (v1 and v2, read through a summarising fetch) say the models were used for literature search, code, testing hypotheses, devising computational strategies, checking and proofreading, and that AI 'accelerated a large part of our work, particularly the computations'. The authors' text I read does not describe the surface step. The press account is a lead, not the authors' account.

Epoch AI lists the M23 problem as 'Solved (human + AI)', says the three models 'first solved the problem', and cites 'comments from the authors' that AI 'was instrumental in solving this problem'. The authors' text names the same three models only in a list of supporting tasks and says 'No text in this article was written by AI'. Epoch's 'first solved' wording is not the authors'; Epoch's cited comments were not visible to me.

Paderborn release says the winning team discovered more than 143,000 polynomials 'entirely without the use of AI' and, in another sentence, that 'With the help of AI, we were able to develop efficient scripts that made it easier to submit the polynomials'. Scientific American says AI's 'only contribution to the winning team was to write an upload script'. The three statements are compatible only if AI was peripheral to the submissions; the release does not name any system.

Completion of the 25,000 degree-24 groups: 'By July' (Paderborn, 10 Sep 2026) against 'concluded in late August' (Scientific American, 22 Sep 2026). Tao's post set stage one to close 15 Aug 2026. SAIR's own results page was not found.

The model list in the authors' acknowledgements differs between arXiv v1 ('We used Claude Fable 5, Claude Opus 4.8, and ChatGPT 5.6 Sol for searching the literature, code generation, testing hypotheses, ruling out other approaches, devising computational strategies, checking our results, and proofreading our manuscript.') and v2 ('We used Claude Fable 5 and 5.1, Claude Opus 4.8, and ChatGPT 5.6 Sol for searching the literature, generating code, checking results, and proofreading.'). Both were read through a summarising fetch, not raw source. The v2 Use-of-AI paragraph also adds 'AI served as a tool that accelerated a large part of our work, particularly the computations'.

M23 paper's first posting: 9 Aug 2026 on the arXiv listing (v1) against 8 Aug 2026 in the MIT-hosted PDF and MathWorld (search summaries). Scientific American is dated 22 Sep 2026 on its page, while the aiweekly reproduction says 23 Sep.

Stale listings: the Emergentmind page (undated, pre-2026) still gives the M23 question as open. Epoch AI lists it as solved. Wikipedia's inverse Galois article (last edited 29 Aug 2026) lists M23 among realised sporadic groups. These are status listings, not disputes about the mathematics.

summary: Found: the problem is still open in general. The window's main event is the M23 result, arXiv:2608.08538 (Huang, Jackson, Lee, Poonen, Pries, Zhang; v1 9 Aug 2026, v2 7 Oct 2026), which proves M23 is a Galois group over Q with an explicit degree-23 polynomial and completes the sporadic groups. This is one finite group inside a universal question, so it is a positive instance of the existence claim and leaves the universal claim open; I have recorded it as the event, not as a resolution. Checking: the authors verified their final results in Magma and PARI/GP; I found no written reading by anyone outside the author team in about two months (the Epoch AI listing, 'Solved (human + AI)' with tag 'Solid result', is a status listing, not a reading). I did not retrieve the polynomial itself. AI: the authors' acknowledgements name Claude Fable 5, Claude Opus 4.8 and ChatGPT 5.6 Sol (and, in v2 wording, 'Claude Fable 5 and 5.1') for literature search, code, testing hypotheses, devising computational strategies, checking results and proofreading, and state that no text was written by AI. Whether that is load-bearing is the close call: the task list includes 'devising computational strategies' and 'testing hypotheses', but the v2 gloss says AI 'accelerated a large part of our work, particularly the computations', and the authors do not say which step produced the key construction. Scientific American (read directly) says AI agents searched for a surface and a coordinate change; that is press and is not in the authors' text I read. Anthropic provided three-month Claude Max subscriptions (disclosed). The second event is a computational contest, not a result on the universal claim: the SAIR challenge (called 16 Jun 2026, stage one closing 15 Aug) permitted AI tools; a Paderborn release (10 Sep 2026) says all 25,000 transitive groups of degree 24 were realised over Q by July, while Scientific American says late August; the winners claim no AI for the calculations and no model is named. Third, partial results for families of groups: Demeio and Gvirtz-Chen (arXiv:2512.23615, Dec 2025, regular realisations of PSL2(F_{p^2}) under congruence conditions on p; not refereed per a Glasgow listing I did not open). Several other 2025-2026 papers are about different questions and are recorded as discounted: Maire and Sankara (number-field towers), Landesman and Levy (function fields over finite fields), and Debes's survey. Historical events are recorded as the problem's background: Hilbert 1892 (S_n and A_n), Shafarevich 1954 (solvable groups; Schmidt-Wingberg 1999 complete proof), Scholz-Reichardt 1937 (odd p-groups), Shih 1974 and Zywina 2013 (PSL2(F_p)), Zywina 2014 (orthogonal families), Dettweiler-Reiter 2023 (SL families; base field unsettled between two readings), Thompson 1984 and the 1984-89 sporadic work (25 of 26), and the near-miss M23 polynomials over a quartic field (Elkies). Matysiak's 2022 'any field' claim is recorded and discounted: it is false as reported, since it fails over R. Close calls: (a) whether the M23 event moves a quantity the question names (the universal claim) or adds a finite instance; I read it as the latter; (b) whether the AI contribution was load-bearing; (c) whether the Paderborn completion counts for anything beyond degree 24, which I think it does not.
competing_reading: For the M23 event, a reader could treat it as a sub-case of the sporadic groups whose closure is a real advance in the problem's own scope, with the sporadic-group programme counted as a meaningful part of the question. The opposite reading treats it as one more finite instance, leaving the universal claim exactly as open as before. On AI, the authors' own text supports a reading where models were computational aids and checkers, so the construction is human-directed; the press account (AI agents found the surface) supports a reading where a model supplied the load-bearing idea. Epoch's 'first solved' and 'human + AI' label read more like the press account than the authors' text. On the degree-24 completion, one could count it as a settled finite case; the more careful reading is that it covers only groups with a faithful transitive action of degree 24.
what_would_settle_it: (1) The raw arXiv source (TeX) for v1 and v2, to confirm the exact model strings, including whether v2 reads 'Claude Fable 5 and 5.1', and the full Use-of-AI paragraph. (2) The authors' own account of who proposed the surface and the non-rigid triple (a talk write-up, a comment on Epoch's problem page, or a later version). (3) The explicit degree-23 polynomial, with an independent Magma or PARI/GP recomputation of its Galois group and ramification, and a comparison of the v1 and v2 polynomials. (4) SAIR's official status page for the degree-24 contest, with completion dates. (5) Any refereeing, erratum or independent replication of arXiv:2608.08538. (6) Whether the Bromberg preprint on M23 exists, what it proves, and when it appeared.

event.what_happened: Julian Demeio and Damian Gvirtz-Chen, 'Galois Realisations of PSL2(F_{p^2}) via non-unirational Hilbert Irreducibility', arXiv:2512.23615, submitted 29 Dec 2025. Abstract (verbatim as far as the fetch returned it): 'We establish non-unirational versions of Hilbert Irreducibility for all Hilbert modular surfaces which are of K3 type. As an application we prove new instances of the regular Inverse Galois Problem for the simple groups PSL2(F_{p^2}) subject to congruence conditions on p.' Earlier talk (2023, search summary): work in progress.
event.revisions: v1 only (29 Dec 2025, 44 KB), per the arXiv abstract page as fetched.
event.delivers: New regular realisations (the standard meaning of 'regular' is over Q(t), which by Hilbert irreducibility gives extensions of Q) of the simple groups PSL2(F_{p^2}), for primes p satisfying congruence conditions that I did not retrieve. Restriction: one infinite family of simple groups, and only for p in those congruence classes.
event.remains: PSL2(F_{p^2}) for primes p outside the congruence conditions, and every other finite group, including all non-simple groups not covered by other results.
event.time_since_posted: about 9 months (29 Dec 2025 to 10 Oct 2026). A search snippet of the Glasgow eprint record (not opened) lists the work as not refereed.
event.direction: Positive for the groups it covers (existence over Q, via regular realisations).

judgement.why: The statement is universal over all finite groups, so no event is whole. The M23 paper is scored case rather than instances: it realises a hard named group and completes the sporadic simple groups as a class, a genuine restriction of the question rather than a finite search. It is checkable because it exhibits an explicit degree-23 polynomial over Q whose Galois group is recomputable in Magma/PARI, and the polynomial is a witness to the existence claim. On AI, the authors' own quote lists literature search, code, testing hypotheses, ruling out approaches, devising computational strategies, checking and proofreading; none of these is a stated piece of the mathematics in the result, and the claim that an AI agent found the key surface rests on Scientific American, not on the authors, so the role is none. The degree-24 contest is a finite list of groups (instances), with AI used only for an upload script. Function-field, number-field-tower and parametric results are variants; the Elkies and other-field M23 work are variants (not over Q). Matysiak's claim is knocked down by the explicit failure over R.
judgement.doubts: Two close calls. (1) M23 as case vs instances: one group inside a universal statement, but read as closing the sporadic class. (2) M23 AI role none vs assisted: 'devising computational strategies' and the Scientific American account (an AI agent proposed the workable surface) could support assisted if the authors confirm it; Epoch cites unseen author comments calling AI 'instrumental'. The polynomial was not retrieved, and v1/v2 equations may differ. Pre-snapshot classical results are marked digested on the strength of long acceptance; the record did not open the primary papers.
